chief_complaint: Chronic management of ischemic heart disease with medication review and optimization of multimorbidity in an elderly male
history_of_present_illness: The patient is an 80‑year‑old man with a long history of ischemic heart disease following a STEMI in 1993, now maintained on nitroglycerin, beta‑blocker, aspirin, two statins, and a thiazide‑ARB combination. He has stable pre‑diabetes, obesity, anemia, and knee osteoarthritis treated with naproxen. Cognitive decline from Alzheimer’s disease is being managed with tacrine. Social isolation and limited contact are noted, and he works part‑time. Recent vital signs show a low‑normal blood pressure (104/66 mmHg) and a heart rate of 80 bpm. He has had multiple wellness visits but also several emergency encounters, likely related to his cardiac and musculoskeletal conditions. Polypharmacy (8 agents) and duplicate statin therapy raise concern for drug‑related adverse effects.
past_medical_history: Acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction (1993-05-10) resolved; viral sinusitis (resolved 1993-01-05); fractures of wrist (resolved 1993-03-19); full‑time employment periods (resolved 1994-12-02 and 1996-12-20); unemployment (resolved 1995-12-08); drug misuse (resolved 1996-11-22); stress (resolved 1996-11-22); medication review due (resolved 1996-12-13).
